claims.text: Adding 0.5–1 vol% nanoscale Y2O3 particles to a refractory HEA will improve its high-temperature mechanical performance.
The Y2O3 addition will maintain low overall alloy density.
The Y2O3 addition will preserve room-temperature strength.
Mechanical alloying followed by hot consolidation can produce a uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion in the refractory HEA.
Temperatures of approximately 1000–1200 °C are representative of the intended jet-turbine service conditions.
Thermally stable nanoscale oxide particles will act as obstacles to dislocation glide.
Thermally stable nanoscale oxide particles will impede grain-boundary sliding.
A uniform low-volume-fraction oxide dispersion will avoid formation of continuous brittle phases.
The principal strengthening mechanism at elevated temperature will be dispersion strengthening.
Oxide particles will pin dislocations and limit grain-boundary motion at elevated temperature.
Pinning dislocations and limiting grain-boundary motion will reduce high-temperature creep rates.
Controlling oxide-particle size and volume fraction to 0.5–1 vol% will cause negligible alteration of room-temperature mechanical properties.
Relative to an identically processed oxide-free HEA, the oxide-containing alloy will have significantly higher yield strength at 1000–1200 °C.
Relative to an identically processed oxide-free HEA, the oxide-containing alloy will have better creep resistance at 1000–1200 °C.
The oxide-containing alloy will retain room-temperature strength and ductility similar to those of the oxide-free baseline.
The density increase caused by adding 0.5–1 vol% Y2O3 will be negligible.
